I don't have any opponent files to test against, so I'll write approximations of the classic warriors (stone, paper, vampire, snake, g2-clear). I'm weighing whether to put them in a separate directory like /tmp, since the instructions say not to touch the opponent files in warriors/, which doesn't exist yet.

Now I'm sketching out a few classic opponents to test against, starting with stone, paper, vampire, and snake, since no opponent files exist yet.

I'm going through the classic opponents in more detail, and the rule of thumb is that stone and scanner-style warriors struggle against paper. My next step is to weigh bombers with a core clear against scanners, since the win-rate thresholds mean ties don't help me.

I'm dropping the idea of writing elaborate opponents from memory and will just set up a few simple ones to experiment against. A strong modern warrior should handle the basic opponents, and a scanner with SPL/DAT clearing looks promising against stone and simple papers. Since the grader's opponents will differ from mine, I want something robust rather than tuned to my own test set.
No opponent files exist on this machine, so I'll write representative versions of the classic warriors in a scratch dir for testing (leaving `warriors/` untouched).
